text:
Abstract
We investigated whether influenza-related data appears within records associated with Escherichia coli across the data resources accessible here. We queried three complementary sources: the NIAID Data Discovery Engine (NDE) for dataset-level records, the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) for raw sequencing runs, and NCBI GEO for processed expression studies. In NDE, we faceted infectious agent names within Dataset records filtered to species.name "Escherichia coli" and free-text terms (influenza, Influenza A, Influenza B); results were 0. A second NDE raw query confirming the same scope returned 0 records. In ENA, searching E. coli (taxid 562) for study titles containing “influenza” returned 5 sequencing runs in BioProject PRJNA504460, with all runs taxonomically annotated as E. coli and the study titled “In vivo analysis of Influenza A mRNA secondary structures identifies critical regulatory motifs.” In GEO, searching Series (GSE) for “Escherichia coli” and “influenza” returned 4 GSE records; one example (GSE222765) lists multiple taxa including E. coli and is a SuperSeries about respiratory infections. These findings show that while integrated dataset-level indexing (NDE) yields no influenza-tagged E. coli datasets, influenza-related content appears in ENA E. coli records and GEO studies that include E. coli. This matters for cross-domain integration and for researchers seeking influenza-context data within E. coli-associated studies.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli is a model bacterium pervasive in molecular biology and sequencing studies. Influenza viruses (Orthomyxoviridae) are major respiratory pathogens; methodological studies sometimes use bacterial RNA or controls, and multi-organism studies can include E. coli. Determining whether influenza-related content appears within E. coli-designated records clarifies cross-repository indexing and reuse pathways.

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether influenza-related data are present in E. coli-tagged records within the repositories accessible here, and at what level (dataset vs. run vs. processed study).

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: assess the presence of influenza-related signals in records annotated to E. coli. Hypothesis: at least some ENA or GEO records annotated to E. coli include influenza-related study context, even if dataset-level NDE indexing does not reflect it.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We triangulated across: NDE (federated dataset-level index), ENA (raw runs with searchable study titles), and GEO (processed expression Series), to capture influenza mentions within E. coli-associated records at different curation levels.

Materials.
- NDE facets and raw query via functions.nde_facet_counts and functions.nde_raw_query.
- ENA run search via functions.brc_ena_search.
- GEO Series search via functions.geo_search.

Procedures.
- NDE facet counts: functions.nde_facet_counts with fields="infectiousAgent.name", query='species.name:"Escherichia coli" AND (influenza OR "Influenza A" OR "Influenza B")', record_type="Dataset", top_n=50. Provenance URL: https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22+AND+%28influenza+OR+%22Influenza+A%22+OR+%22Influenza+B%22%29%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22&size=0&facets=infectiousAgent.name&facet_size=50
- NDE raw query: functions.nde_raw_query with q='species.name:"Escherichia coli" AND (influenza OR infectiousAgent.name:"Influenza A virus" OR infectiousAgent.name:"Influenza B virus")', size=25, offset=0, fields='name,includedInDataCatalog.name,infectiousAgent.name,species.name,url,identifier', facets='', facet_size=20, summarize=true. Provenance URL: https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22+AND+%28influenza+OR+infectiousAgent.name%3A%22Influenza+A+virus%22+OR+infectiousAgent.name%3A%22Influenza+B+virus%22%29&size=25&_source=name%2CincludedInDataCatalog.name%2CinfectiousAgent.name%2Cspecies.name%2Curl%2Cidentifier
- ENA search: functions.brc_ena_search with taxonomy_id="562", title_contains="influenza", limit=100. Provenance URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search (params: query='tax_eq(562) AND study_title="*influenza*"', limit=100)
- GEO Series search: functions.geo_search with organism="Escherichia coli", term="influenza", entry_type="gse", max_results=20. Provenance URL: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi (params: db=gds, term='"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND (influenza) AND "gse"[Filter]', retmax=20)

Statistical Analysis.
- NDE facet counts: matching_records=0 and facet totals derived from facets.infectiousAgent.name (total_with_field=0).
- NDE raw query: total=0 returned; interpreted as 0 records.
- ENA search: total_matching=5 (reported directly by the tool) for tax_eq(562) and study_title containing “influenza”.
- GEO search: total_count=4 and returned=4 for Series (GSE) with organism “Escherichia coli” and term “influenza”. Counts reflect NCBI’s query translation to MeSH, as reported.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Summary of influenza-related signals within E. coli-associated records.

| Source | Query scope | Result count | Notes | Provenance URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NDE (Dataset facet) | species.name:"Escherichia coli" AND (influenza OR "Influenza A" OR "Influenza B") | 0 | No infectiousAgent facet values returned | https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22+AND+%28influenza+OR+%22Influenza+A%22+OR+%22Influenza+B%22%29%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22&size=0&facets=infectiousAgent.name&facet_size=50 |
| NDE (Dataset raw) | species.name:"Escherichia coli" AND (influenza OR infectiousAgent.name:"Influenza A virus" OR infectiousAgent.name:"Influenza B virus") | 0 | No dataset-level matches | https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22+AND+%28influenza+OR+infectiousAgent.name%3A%22Influenza+A+virus%22+OR+infectiousAgent.name%3A%22Influenza+B+virus%22%29&size=25&_source=name%2CincludedInDataCatalog.name%2CinfectiousAgent.name%2Cspecies.name%2Curl%2Cidentifier |
| ENA runs | tax_eq(562) AND study_title contains "influenza" | 5 | All runs taxid=562 (E. coli); study PRJNA504460 title references Influenza A | https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search |
| GEO Series (GSE) | Organism "Escherichia coli" AND term "influenza" | 4 | Example: GSE222765 SuperSeries with multiple taxa including E. coli | https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi |

Findings.
- NDE dataset-level queries returned 0 matching records for E. coli with influenza terms.
- ENA returned 5 E. coli runs whose study title includes “influenza.”
- GEO returned 4 Series records with E. coli and the term “influenza.”

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The absence of NDE dataset-level matches indicates no datasets formally indexed as E. coli with influenza infectious agent tags in the federated catalog. However, ENA’s run-level search identified 5 E. coli runs in a study explicitly referencing Influenza A mRNA structures, and GEO identified 4 Series records where E. coli appears alongside influenza-related terms. Thus, influenza-related context occurs within E. coli-associated records at run- and study-level granularity.

Context. ENA results (PRJNA504460) show sequencing runs annotated to E. coli in a study title about influenza RNA structures, suggesting methodological or control use of E. coli RNA in influenza-focused work. GEO’s GSE222765 SuperSeries includes E. coli among multiple taxa in a respiratory infection context, consistent with broad antigen panels or cross-species content.

Limitations.
- NDE indexing may not capture study-title mentions or multi-organism contexts; 0 matches reflect dataset-level metadata, not sample-level content.
- ENA study titles are submitter free text; presence of “influenza” does not on its own establish influenza sequences in E. coli samples.
- GEO query translation via MeSH broadens “influenza” to “influenza, human,” which can include studies where E. coli is ancillary.
- Counts reflect current index states and query scopes; we did not enumerate all samples or files within studies.

Conclusion & Future Directions. Influenza-related context exists in E. coli-associated records in ENA and GEO, despite no dataset-level matches in the federated NDE index. Next steps: inspect PRJNA504460 in ENA to confirm sample content and aims; retrieve GEO Series details per accession (geo_series) to identify which components include E. coli and influenza-specific assays; broaden NDE search via semantic_search for natural-language matches; and, if needed, search ENA by experiment titles or sample attributes.

References
[1] NIAID Data Discovery Engine (NDE) facet counts. https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22+AND+%28influenza+OR+%22Influenza+A%22+OR+%22Influenza+B%22%29%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22&size=0&facets=infectiousAgent.name&facet_size=50
[2] NIAID Data Discovery Engine (NDE) raw query. https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=species.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22+AND+%28influenza+OR+infectiousAgent.name%3A%22Influenza+A+virus%22+OR+infectiousAgent.name%3A%22Influenza+B+virus%22%29&size=25&_source=name%2CincludedInDataCatalog.name%2CinfectiousAgent.name%2Cspecies.name%2Curl%2Cidentifier
[3] European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) portal search. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search
[4] NCBI GEO esearch (GDS). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi

Acknowledgments
We thank the NIAID Data Discovery Engine, the European Nucleotide Archive, and NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus for providing the indexed records used in this analysis.
